property_summary: For any initialize(...) arguments the reference contract stores baseToken equal to the provided _baseToken parameter; the mutant that unconditionally sets baseToken = address(0) will cause this equality to fail for some fuzzed _baseToken (e.g. any non-zero address).

For any inputs to initialize, the deployed C sets its public baseToken exactly to the provided _baseToken argument; the mutant sets baseToken to the factory address instead, so for some fuzzed _baseToken values the stored baseToken will differ.

For any inputs to initialize, the contract's public baseToken getter must equal the _baseToken argument passed; the mutant that assigns baseToken = _nft violates this (for some inputs baseToken != _baseToken).

For any inputs to initialize(...) the deployed contract's public nft() getter equals the _nft argument passed (the reference sets nft = _nft on initialize); the mutant that omits that assignment can leave nft() different from the passed _nft for some inputs.

For any initialize(...) call on a fresh C, the contract's public nft() equals the _nft argument passed (reference preserves the supplied NFT address); the mutant that sets nft = address(0) breaks this rule for some inputs.

For any inputs to initialize the reference contract stores nft equal to the _nft argument (i.e. c.nft() == _nft after initialize); the mutant that swaps assignments breaks this (there exists inputs where c.nft() != _nft).

For all inputs to initialize, the stored changeFee equals the provided _changeFee (i.e. c.changeFee() == _changeFee); the mutant that stores _changeFee - 1 will violate this for any _changeFee != 0 (and revert when _changeFee == 0), so some fuzzed inputs will make the mutant fail this property.

For any _feeRate input within the allowed range, calling initialize(...) sets c.feeRate() equal to the provided _feeRate; the mutant that adds 1 to assignment will cause c.feeRate() != _feeRate for some fuzzed _feeRate inputs.

For any input to initialize, the deployed contract's public feeRate equals the _feeRate argument passed (reference preserves the supplied fee rate); the mutant that assigns feeRate = 0 breaks this by making feeRate always zero for some nonzero _feeRate inputs.

For every input call to initialize(...) the reference contract accepts any feeRate in [0,5000] (i.e. initialize does not revert and sets feeRate to the provided value); the mutant wrongly rejects feeRate == 0 causing initialize to revert for some admissible input.

For any valid initialize(...) call that succeeds, the reference contract always sets initialized == true after the call; the mutant omits setting initialized so for some inputs initialize returns but initialized remains false, violating this invariant.

For any valid initialize(...) call on a fresh C, the contract's public boolean `initialized` becomes true after the call returns; the mutant that sets `initialized = false` at end breaks this by leaving it false for some inputs.

For any valid initialize(...) arguments, calling initialize exactly once on a fresh C should succeed (no revert) and leave c.initialized() == true; the mutant that sets initialized = true before the AlreadyInitialized check can cause initialize to always revert (making the call fail) for some inputs/contexts, breaking this property.

For any admissible initialize(...) arguments, on a fresh contract the first call to initialize(...) must succeed (return normally) and set initialized()==true, while the mutant may make the call revert (so the call does not succeed) for some inputs because it sets initialized=true before checking AlreadyInitialized().

For any admissible initialize(...) arguments, calling initialize exactly once on a fresh C must return normally (not revert) and afterwards c.initialized() == true; the mutant can make initialize revert by setting initialized = true before the AlreadyInitialized check, so for some inputs the call will fail and the property will not hold.

For any input arguments, calling initialize(...) on a fresh C instance must succeed (not revert) and leave c.initialized() == true; the mutant that sets initialized = true before checking AlreadyInitialized can cause initialize to revert (breaking the rule) for some inputs.
